Synopsis:
The player reads a bronze plaque at the feet of a mysterious statue

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_SqueletonRoom.json: You and your party are standing in a dim, neglected tomb chamber before a weathered statue (or sarcophagus) with a worn bronze plaque at its base; age, grime, poor light or an unfamiliar script are obscuring the inscription. The group likely reached this room after traversing the tomb’s corridors and hazards, and reading the plaque may require an Investigation/Perception or language/Religion check or a companion’s lore to render the text. Companions (commonly Shadowheart or a scholar) might offer translations or note they don’t recognize the patron, and the plaque could contain names, dates, warnings, ritual details, or clues that advance quest text or trigger an environmental reaction. The player’s mocking pronunciation of “Selûne” and the question about who was worshipped here simply reflect that the inscription is indecipherable to them at the moment.

The plaque’s inscription is obscured by age—fading, grime, corrosion, poor lighting, or an unfamiliar script—so the game often requires an Investigation/Perception or language/lore check to make out the words. Companions, scholars, or an unseen narrator may offer translations, lore, warnings, or practical help (or note that the text is illegible). Reading the plaque could reveal names, dates, rituals, or clues relevant to the tomb and may advance quest text or trigger a reaction from the environment.
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_SanctumStatue.json: You are standing inside a tomb before a worn bronze plaque set at the feet of an unidentified statue, trying to make out an inscription obscured by grime, corrosion, or an unfamiliar script. The plaque’s language may be unknown to you — the narration or your character can note you “do not recognise” it — so the game often requires an Investigation/Perception or language/lore check to decipher it. If companions or an NPC scholar are present they might offer translations or commentary (or a narrator might give a brief rendering); otherwise the text may be presented as an interpreted description. The plaque likely contains names, dates, warnings, ritual details, or clues relevant to the tomb and reading it can advance knowledge, trigger quest text, or provoke an environmental reaction; the player’s line can be skeptical or mocking while speculating about a dedication to a forgotten god.
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_TrappedTomb.json: The scene takes place inside a tomb where the player is examining a bronze plaque whose inscription is in an unfamiliar script. The narrator explicitly notes the text is a mystery, so off-screen the party lacks the means (knowledge, a scholar, or a translation spell) to read it. The player's spoken line is a speculative inference that the inscription refers to an ancient cult or deity, not a revealed fact.
- CHA_Crypt_VB_Sanctum_2_WithShadowheart.json: You and your party have entered an old tomb-chapel chamber dominated by a worn statue with a bronze plaque at its base; the room is dust-filled and evidently abandoned. The plaque’s inscription is obscured by grime, corrosion, fading, or an unfamiliar script, and the narration/scene makes clear the party currently lacks the means (a scholar, a translation spell, or a successful lore/language check) to read it. Shadowheart, a cleric in the party, voices puzzlement that she can’t identify the statue’s patron — a tentative, in-world observation rather than a definitive fact. Deciphering the plaque (via investigation or translation) could reveal names, rituals, warnings, or other clues that advance the tomb’s story or provoke an environmental reaction.
